verdict.rationale: ROS 2 gives a strong starting point for bring-up. The project says it covers everything 'from drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms', and the docs show a launch system for coordinating nodes, parameters, CLI introspection, and Gazebo simulation. Community users add that existing nodes and drivers, plus teleop, bagging and visualization, come largely 'for free' and take you 'from nothing to something faster than anything'. However, hands-on users also report dependency hell, a convoluted build system, disorganized tutorials and weird errors, which undercuts the 'hours rather than weeks' promise. Missing for 10: documented hardware abstraction or driver-integration workflow, robot description and configuration tooling, an evidenced path to first motion on real hardware, and independent reports of fast bring-up times.
